traceability.notes: docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md is a concrete implementation spec for improved error reporting. The referenced rules and helpers implement specific, templated error messages with ESLint-standard meta.messages and data placeholders for function names, file paths, requirement IDs, and detailed validation context. The require-story-annotation rule uses coreReportMissing/coreReportMethod to provide specific messages, structured data ({ name, functionName }) and ESLint suggestions, which are validated in tests/rules/error-reporting.test.ts. The require-req-annotation rule exposes a matching missingReq message and uses a shared annotation-checker helper to report with the same data shape, covered by tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts. Branch-level errors use the shared 'Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}.' pattern across @story/@req with tested autofix behavior. Format and reference rules (valid-annotation-format, valid-story-reference, valid-req-reference) centralize their messages using {{details}}, {{path}}, {{reqId}}, and {{storyPath}} placeholders and are thoroughly exercised by their respective test suites, including error-handling cases where filesystem or configuration context is incomplete. Severity conventions are encoded in TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES and surfaced via the recommended/strict configs, with tests explicitly verifying that missing annotations and unresolved references are treated as errors, while annotation-format issues are warnings. All relevant tests, including the dedicated error-reporting test suite and config/severity tests, pass under the project’s Jest run. Collectively, this provides strong, concrete evidence that all acceptance criteria and listed requirements for story 007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING are fully implemented and verified.
